messages:
anya: Quick heads-up — after switching the reranker to pairwise objective + PTQ (8-bit), we're seeing NDCG@10 drop ~4.2% on the validation slice. Not sure if it's quantization, pairwise sampling, or eval mismatch. Anyone seen this pattern?

matt: Can you paste the eval command and the exact numbers? Also which slice — titles, short queries, long queries?

anya: Eval snippet below. This is on the benchmark 'prod-search-aug' holdout (100k queries) with full-doc scoring.

```
# eval command
python -m eval.run --model reranker-v2-pairwise-ptq8 --dataset prod-search-aug --split holdout --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --format docs_full --batch 256
```

Results (latest run):
```
Model: reranker-v2-fp16 (baseline)  -> NDCG@10: 0.412  MRR: 0.278
Model: reranker-v2-pairwise-ptq8  -> NDCG@10: 0.395  MRR: 0.275
```

So MRR barely changed, but NDCG drop is consistent across 3 runs.

matt: Hm. MRR stable but NDCG down suggests tail ranking shuffled more than top-1. Pairwise loss can shift ordering for lower-ranked docs. But PTQ could also be skewing logits in subtle ways.

sara: Two quick checks: 1) Are your eval logits calibrated? PTQ sometimes compresses score range, affecting listwise/ndcg more than mrr. 2) Confirm that training used the same doc formatting (we had a bug where training used `title + snippet`, eval used `title + full doc`).

anya: Good call. Training config was `title | snippet` (we added a pipe token in preprocessing), but eval used `title + \n + content` without the pipe. Will re-run with matching preproc.

jen: Also verify the pairwise sampling temperature. If negative pairs were chosen differently during train vs eval population, you can get distribution shift. We had a case where sampling used cached negatives (hard negatives) for training but eval expects in-batch negatives. That inflates pairwise margins.

anya: Copying that. Another datapoint: ran bucketed analysis by query length (quick summary):

```
Buckets: short(<=3 tok), mid(4-12), long(>12)
Baseline NDCG@10: short 0.423, mid 0.410, long 0.390
PTQ pairwise: short 0.418, mid 0.396, long 0.369
```

Drop worst on long queries. Could be kv-cache truncation or tokenization differences.

matt: If long queries are hit harder, check attention pattern changes after PTQ. Also confirm `max_input_len` during quantized inference — some kernels drop tokens beyond a threshold silently.

anya: Will check max_input_len and tokenizer version. One weirdness: locally using GPU kernel `quant-kernel-v3` gives slightly better NDCG than `quant-kernel-v2` (both PTQ) — so kernel selection matters.

eval-bot: CI eval report uploaded: https://ci.internal/reports/1802345678. Summary attached:
- reranker-v2-fp16: NDCG@10=0.412 +-0.002
- reranker-v2-pairwise-ptq8 (kernel v2): NDCG@10=0.395 +-0.003
- reranker-v2-pairwise-ptq8 (kernel v3): NDCG@10=0.401 +-0.002

jen: Interesting — kernel v3 recovers ~60% of the gap. Suggests numerical kernel differences. Also run a single-listwise fine-tune (small LR) on PTQ outputs to re-calibrate scores, or apply a simple affine rescaling of logits as a cheap fix.

sara: For the dataset side: re-run a small eval where you reformat eval docs to `title|snippet` to match training. If that recovers most of the gap we've found the root cause.

anya: Plan: 1) reformat eval to exactly match training preproc and re-run on kernel v3 (run tonight), 2) test max_input_len and tokenizer versions, 3) run quick affine calibration on logits and measure NDCG uplift. I'll post results tomorrow. Thanks all :pray:

matt: Sounds good. If you need a lightweight script for affine calibration, ping me; I have one (in `eng-ml/tools/calibrate_logits.py`).

anya: @matt yep will grab it. Closing loop tomorrow with numbers.
